stem: Which transition best fits the blank?
stimulus: When a reservoir in a semi-arid basin kept shrinking even in years of normal rainfall, hydrologists installed sensors along its shoreline and outlet channels. Their measurements pointed to one dominant cause of the loss. ______, evaporation from the reservoir's broad, shallow surface accounted for nearly 60 percent of the water that disappeared each summer, far more than the water released downstream or the water seeping into the ground.
explanation: The sentence before says the measurements found one dominant cause. The sentence after names that cause, evaporation, and gives its size. There is no larger group of causes being sampled here. You are zooming in on the single cause already mentioned, so the relationship is specification, and "Specifically" expresses it.

B.why: You treated specification as if it were an example. "For example" presents one item out of several, but the passage says there was one dominant cause. The next sentence restates that single cause more precisely. It doesn't pick one cause from a list.

C.why: You read the evaporation figure as a surprise and took the surprise for disagreement. The second sentence doesn't contradict the first. It spells out the cause the first sentence mentions, so a contrast word doesn't fit.

D.why: You picked a cause-and-effect word, but finding a dominant cause doesn't make evaporation account for 60 percent of the loss. The second sentence says what the finding was. It isn't a result of the finding.

stem: Which word or phrase best fits the blank in context?
stimulus: Parrotfish are best known as grazers. By scraping algae off coral reefs with their beaklike teeth, they keep fast-growing algae from smothering slower-growing corals. ______, parrotfish are major producers of sand. Fragments of coral scraped up during feeding are ground down in the fish's throat and excreted as fine white grains, and on some reefs these grains make up much of the sand on nearby beaches.
explanation: The first part describes one important thing parrotfish do: they control algae. The next sentence adds a second, separate thing they do: they make sand. The fact is unexpected, but it doesn't clash with the first. You could put "and also" between the two ideas and it would still sound right, so the relationship is same direction, which "Moreover" signals.

B.why: You mistook a surprising sentence for a contradicting one. Making sand doesn't undo or dispute the grazing role. It's a second role added to the first, so a contrast word is wrong.

C.why: You chose an example word, but sand production isn't an example of keeping algae off corals. It's a different activity, so it can't be a sample of the grazing role described before it.

D.why: You chose a restatement word, but the second sentence doesn't say the first idea again in different terms. Producing sand is new information, not a rewording of controlling algae.

stem: Which transition belongs in the blank?
stimulus: Over three winters, ecologists studying a flock of dark-eyed juncos brushed the snow off half of the ground plots where the birds fed, leaving seeds on those plots exposed. The other plots were left snow-covered. ______, birds feeding in the cleared plots spent roughly a third less time foraging each day than birds feeding in the untouched plots, freeing hours for resting and preening.
explanation: The first sentences describe what the researchers did: they uncovered the seeds on some plots. The sentence after the blank describes what happened because of it: birds on those plots needed less time to find food. The first action produced the second outcome, so the relationship is cause and effect, and "As a result" is the match.

B.why: You chose a same-direction word that signals a parallel case. The second sentence isn't a situation like the first one. It's the outcome of the first one, so the link is cause, not similarity.

C.why: You chose a word that means "despite this." Birds foraging less when seeds were easy to reach is exactly what you'd expect from clearing the snow. Nothing in the second sentence goes against the first.

D.why: You chose an example word, but reduced foraging time isn't an instance of brushing snow off plots. It's what followed from doing that, so the relationship is cause, not example.

stem: Which choice best fills the blank?
stimulus: A training manual widely used by youth soccer clubs recommends agility-ladder drills as a way to make players faster. ______, the drills did produce modest improvements in sprint times among players in a recent twelve-week trial. Those improvements, however, disappeared within three weeks of the drills being dropped, and players who practiced short, all-out sprints instead improved about twice as much.
explanation: The sentence after the blank grants a point in the manual's favor: the drills did help a little. The next sentence then turns against the drills with "however." Granting a point before disputing it is concession. The reversal really comes, so "Admittedly" fits.

B.why: You chose a cause-and-effect word, but a manual recommending the drills didn't cause the drills to improve sprint times. The trial's results are evidence about the recommendation. They aren't a consequence of it.

C.why: You chose a contrast word, but modest gains in speed support the manual's claim that the drills make players faster. The contrast in this passage comes in the following sentence, not at this blank.

D.why: You chose a specification word, but the trial results don't restate the manual's recommendation more precisely. They report what happened when the recommendation was tested, and they set up a point conceded before it's challenged.
